11bb697ec74ff8bedc5d4284110aef0a6169afd8.summary: The GReAT team reports the EastWind campaign, first detected in late July 2024. Phishing emails with malicious shortcut attachments reached dozens of computers at Russian government organizations and IT companies. The malware used Dropbox for commands and loaded further tools: a GrewApacha RAT that the report links to APT31, an updated CloudSorcerer backdoor, and a new PlugY implant that the report says shares code with DRBControl, which several companies link to APT27.

11fcd89425219e6f04a62fc062c9284bbb39ac82.summary: Huntress analyses a macOS intrusion that began on June 11, 2025 at a cryptocurrency foundation. The attack used a fake Zoom meeting with deepfakes and a malicious AppleScript. Huntress attributes it with high confidence to the North Korean subgroup BlueNoroff, also tracked as TA444. Eight malicious binaries were recovered: a Go backdoor, Nim implants, a process-injection loader, an Objective-C keylogger that also captures screens and clipboard, and a Go crypto-wallet infostealer.

The actor used SQL injection to run PowerShell, an antivirus process check, and a download of the Demux loader. CrowdStrike Intelligence assessed with low confidence that CARBON SPIDER was behind it. The blog says the threat was contained in under 30 minutes and the host fully remediated within 1 hour and 45 minutes.

1137d574278dedd79c844634a5d5239640fa5f40.summary: Paul Jung of Excellium's CERT-XLM team (Virus Bulletin 2020) describes a December 2019 incident at a Belgian healthcare actor. The ransom operation was allegedly run by TA505. Attackers sent phishing emails leading to a macro-enabled Word document, deployed the GET2 dropper and the SDBbot backdoor, then used TinyMet, smbexec and credential dumping to take over a domain controller and plant SDBbot on more than 50 hosts. The responders contained the intrusion 21 days after the breach. The report also maps SDBbot command servers, finding 11 running servers in June 2020.
